page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the ARM64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores using the Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per core. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data reveals average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, alongside average large-block memory read and write bandwidth. However, the instance exhibits weak performance in several areas, including Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, software compilation, and static web serving throughput. Cryptographic and LLM inference capabilities are particularly limited, with poor results in Passmark CPU encryption and small-model LLM text generation.

The t2a-standard-4 offers a power-efficient ARM hardware profile suitable for general-purpose workloads such as database operations, lightweight web serving, and ARM64 application development. The lack of AVX instruction sets and dedicated local storage represents a clear tradeoff, making it less suitable for high-performance computing, intensive cryptography, or large-scale data processing.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities in stress-ng CPU tests and database operations, but show weaknesses in single-threaded compression, software compilation, and static web serving. Cryptographic and LLM inference tasks perform poorly due to the lack of specialized instruction sets like AVX.
